HRA Analysis: OVERVIEW: HOME AND DRY (3) got back into the winner’s circle last start at Cranbourne. He flashed home impressively from midfield up the straight to win well. This race is harder, but he now has the winning confidence. KIMCHI (4) has a good turn of foot, including good gate speed, which he has the option to use here. THE IRISHMAN (2) has had some really tough or unlucky runs recently. He often gets caught wide and needs to cover extra ground racing wide. Last start was his first run in some time where he had a good trip, but he looked to underperform a bit there. From barrier two, he should have some luck. THEROUX (6) is a nice horse who is always competitive. He should be peak fit now as it’s his fourth start back this prep. Tricky barrier. Also respecting NORMANDY NUGGET (1) from the barrier. SELECTIONS:HOME AND DRY (3), KIMCHI (4), THE IRISHMAN (2), THEROUX (6)

OVERVIEW: NIGHT FLIGHT (8) returned with a fourth last start at Melton. He was held up late but hit the line well, and it was a harder race than this one. He will improve with fitness. He always runs well at this track, but he will need some luck from the barrier. JOE LOU (4) is in flying form. He’s won four of his last seven and finished second in the other two. PURPLE MOON (2) has had three starts in the state for a second and two fifths. Last start, she was fifth in the Vicbred Super Series 3yo Silver Trot, which was a tougher race than this. She led on that occasion. She is likely to find the front again here. JILLIBY RADIANCE (5) tired last start in the Group 1 Vicbred Super Series Final. However, it was a terrific result to qualify for the race. In her heat, she contested for the lead and galloped out of the field, caught up and hit the line impressively for fourth. A big winning chance here if she trots throughout and brings her best. Also respecting SHAQ THE ANVIL (1) from the barrier. SELECTIONS:NIGHT FLIGHT (8), JOE LOU (4), PURPLE MOON (2), JILLIBY RADIANCE (1).

OVERVIEW: A SPECIAL OCCASION (8) is a Captaintreacherous-sired three-year-old from New Zealand having his first Australian start for trainer-driver Michael Stanley. He trialled at Melton earlier this month, where he ran home in a fast 26.6 final quarter for the middle trip. He has strong New Zealand form, including a third in the Group 1 Northern Derby, where he stormed home from four fence. He can get off the fence being the only horse on the back row here and will be hard to beat. COOL STORY (3) has been racing well, but he does lack early gate speed, so he often needs to make his own luck. He’s a nice horse, and I’m respecting the Ross Graham-James Herbertson combo here. TEST OF FIRE (2) has brilliant gate speed and won by 25.8 metres at this track two starts ago after leading. However, he is first-up here, so fitness will be a query. MY MARIONETTE (1) has the best sectional times on exposed Australian form in this event. She should get a good trip from barrier one. SELECTIONS: A SPECIAL OCCASION (8), COOL STORY (3), TEST OF FIRE (2), MY MARIONETTE (1)

OVERVIEW: CHILLHUNNYBUNNY (4) was first-up in five months last start when second at Ballarat. She ran home nicely behind No Telling Heather. She will improve on that run with fitness. MAORI TATTOO (6) flashed home nicely into third last start at Maryborough. He has been racing well recently, he just needs some luck from the barrier and to get his manners right. BROOKLYNGOTCOURAGE (2) can get it wrong with her manners, but when she does everything right and gets some luck, she can perform well. Barrier two suits. IM MISS ROYALTY (8) has the best sectional times in this event but is first-up here since July. Also respecting SNICKERS EXPRESS (7) here. He’s good enough to be a winning chance here, but his barrier makes it tricky. BACK: CHILLHUNNYBUNNY (4) – 2 units (win) SELECTIONS:CHILLHUNNYBUNNY (4), MAORI TATTOO (6), BROOKLYNGOTCOURAGE (2), IM MISS ROYALTY (8)

OVERVIEW: ULTIMATE GRANGE (7) is having his second career start here. On debut, he went back to last and got held up but did everything right and ran home well. He will improve from the run with experience but has an awkward barrier again here. CALIFORNIA COOL (3) is having his third career start here. He ran a solid third last start behind Le Gaston and Storm Vendetta. He performed well, and I can imagine he will be a maiden for long. RIDE HIGH CAPTIN (2) led last start and was beaten late by the smart King Baldwin. He should be able to map well here from barrier two. ZAV DAN (5) has been racing OK but has a tricky barrier to contend with here. SELECTIONS:ULTIMATE GRANGE (7), CALIFORNIA COOL (3), RIDE HIGH CAPTIN (2), ZAV DAN (5)

OVERVIEW: EL TORNADO (3) is a nice trotter who found his best form last start. He did some work early and then ran home well late to win impressively. He has the winning confidence now. CONSTANT (6) was a well-deserved winner last start at Kilmore. She’s been racing so well and has a great turn of foot. Barrier six is awkward here, but she is a good winning chance again if she has some luck. WHY NOT (2) will get a good trip now with the scratching from barrier one. He’s only had the four career starts but looks to be a talented type. WHISKEY DAWN (7) is an interesting trotter. She clearly has ability and has run some nice races in her short career. She also hasn’t had the best luck and can get it wrong with her manners. It will be tough from barrier seven here, but a win also wouldn’t surprise. BACK: EL TORNADO (3) – 2.5 units (win) SELECTIONS:EL TORNADO (3), CONSTANT (6), WHY NOT (2), WHISKEY DAWN (7)

OVERVIEW: MISS ADDI (7) is a smart mare who has only missed a place once in her career. She flashed home into second two starts ago at Melton and followed that up with a win last start at Cranbourne after finding the front. She may not have luck here from the barrier, but her class will likely still shine through. MY ATLANTIS (2) is third-up here after over a year on the sidelines, so expecting an improved performance here with fitness. Last start, she wasn’t pushed at Geelong but seemed to run home OK. From the barrier, she should perform well. STORM VENDETTA (4) has run two good seconds in his last two starts. He raced in the breeze and battled on well for second last start. He can race well again here. STEEL MIKI (5) returns here first-up since March. He was a good winner in the breeze last start before his break at Swan Hill. He is lightly raced and appears like a horse who will improve with age, so I am expecting an even better preparation from him this time in. BACK: MISS ADDI (7) – 2.5 units (win) SELECTIONS: MISS ADDI (7), MY ATLANTIS (2), STORM VENDETTA (4), STEEL MIKI (5)

OVERVIEW: THEMIDNIGHTEXPRESS (2) is a smart horse who qualified for the Group 1 APG Vicbred Super Series Final last start, but a racing incident from the first attempt saw him scratched. However, he is racing really well, has the gate speed to find the front and has the best sectional times in this event. He will be hard to beat. MATRIARCH DAISY (4) is lightly raced, but at her best she is a nice horse. If she relies on her speed here and is saved for one run, she could be flashing home nicely late. MAJOR ROY (5) is third-up here and will be close to peak race fitness. He was held up late last start but looked to be hitting the line really well. IM THE REASON (3) is first-up here after two Maryborough trial victories. He has ability at his best. BACK: THEMIDNIGHTEXPRESS (2) – 3 units (win) SELECTIONS:THEMIDNIGHTEXPRESS (2), MATRIARCH DAISY (4), MAJOR ROY (5), IM THE REASON (3) Harness.org.au Help Privacy Advertise Terms Of Use Contact Us © Racing Information Services Enterprise 2026 Powered by

LITTLE CAPPUCCINA (2) looks to get her chance to break through after a run of placings of late. She should be first to the pegs over the short mile distance, which should suit. ARRIVAL TIME (4) looks the main other gate-speed horse in the field and was driven confidently from a wide draw first up in the state, battling on okay over the middle distance. The Todd Rattray-trained pair LETHAL REPLICA (3) and YASTREMSKA LEIS (6) have been consistent and continue to improve throughout their short careers. Both would appreciate some tempo from the runners mentioned above to help their chances of finishing home strongly, even in the small field. CRUNCHTHEGUN (1) gets the nice pole draw and wouldn't surprise if he bobbed up provided he paces cleanly throughout, while ARKAIDA (5) would need to improve on exposed form to be in the finish. Selections:LITTLE CAPPUCCINA (2), ARRIVAL TIME (4), LETHAL REPLICA (3), YASTREMSKA LEIS (6)

The second small field of maidens, this time for the four-year-old and older horses, looks a somewhat competitive affair. Expect LIFE ONA HIGHWAY (2) to show his usual gate speed, be first to the pegs and run along at an even tempo, which should mean DIAMONDONTHEROCKS (1) gets his chance up the sprint lane if, in fact, he doesn't hold the lead himself. IDEN ELIZA JANE (5) also possesses some gate speed and could be another that runs the gate, so despite the small field, we could see some genuine early tempo. If that eventuates, UNOBETTER (3) looks the one to be finishing off strongly and is getting closer with every start to breaking through. SOHO PINA COLADA (6) is a 15-start maiden but hasn't been far away of late despite doing some work. She would also appreciate the runners up front going to war to help bring her into the finish. VOODOO RANGER (4) continues to earn cheques in this maiden grade and should again be thereabouts. Selections:UNO BETTER (3), LIFE ONA HIGHWAY (2), DIAMONDONTHEROCKS (1), IDEN ELIZA JANE (5)

The low-class race over the middle distance brings together the usual customers. Expect BARBETTE (3) to have a good crack at being first to the pegs with her handy gate speed, while the remainder of the speed map is quite tricky to figure out. KIAVINO STRIDE (9) could be the one to make a mid-race move from the trailing back-row draw, while HORRIE OTARA (5) could be another that works his way forward from the gate. MIDNITE DESIRE (2) has been somewhat disappointing since arriving in the state, failing to finish off after receiving nice runs in transit, but again gets his chance from the soft draw. SWEET AMOUR (6) wasn't far away first up for the new stable after doing all the work outside the leader last start. STAROFREMEMBRANCE (7) and QUEENOFDANCE (8) can never be discounted in a field like this, as they're always capable of running home strongly and will again be relying on some solid tempo up front to bring them into the finish. HALIS BOY (1) is first up from a break for a new stable without a trial, so the market may be the best guide to his chances. Selections:SWEET AMOUR (6), BARBETTE (3), QUEENOFDANCE (8), MIDNITE DESIRE (2)

PARK LANE (4) should use his sharp gate speed to zoom straight to the front over the short distance. He clearly hasn't been finishing off his races at his best over the past few months, but should get every opportunity in front here. MODERN JIVE (1) and COUNT YOUR BLESSIN (2) should find positions on speed with cover from their favourable draws. Expect MY BEAUTIFUL LIFE (6) may push forward from her somewhat wide gate over the short distance. Her recent Victorian form has only been fair, but she was very competitive when racing in Tasmania earlier in the year, and a return to that form would make her hard to beat in this field. FEELINKINDALUCKY (7) has been consistent of late but strikes the outside front-row draw, while NO NUKES SKIPPER (8) and KUHIO CREST (5) will be relying on some genuine tempo to allow them to finish home strongly and be in the finish at odds. Selections:MY BEAUTIFUL LIFE (6), FEELINKINDALUCKY (7), MODERN JIVE (1), KUHIO CREST (5)

IDEN OLIVER (2) looks very well graded in this race with Grace Jones's claim. He put together a string of victories before a handy fourth last start when coming from back in the field, and expect he will take a power of beating in this class of race. We may see some gate speed from DENNY (6) and KARALTA ARTEMIS (7) over the mile, although both would need to improve on recent efforts to be in the finish, noting the latter has since undergone a stable change. KNOCK OUT (1) should also look to find a forward position from the pole draw. CAN FEEL THE FURY (5) looks the pick of the Wayne Yole-trained runners and should appreciate some genuine speed throughout, while DONNY IN PARIS (8) should get a soft run along the pegs and could be the knockout hope if clear running appears late. Selections:IDEN OLIVER (2), CAN FEEL THE FURY (5), DONNY IN PARIS (8), KNOCKOUT (1)

The biggest field of the day brings together a competitive bunch, where expect SOHO TIGER LILY (5) to use her usual sharp gate speed to attempt to find, and likely be first to, the pegs. MAXX (6) should also push forward from his wide gate, with only fair gate speed shown by most of those drawn inside, apart from ROCKNROLL MCCRAE (1), who should find a forward position from the pole draw. TAPPY (7) looks the most progressive horse in the field, strikes an awkward draw in a big field and will require a good drive to get her into the finish. LADY IN LINE (10) has winning form to her name and should again be running home strongly, as she consistently does. KENYA (13) is normally driven aggressively but draws the car park here, so it will be interesting to see whether they adopt his usual tactics from well back in the field. Selections: MAXX (6), TAPPY (7), SOHO TIGERLILY (5), LADY IN LINE (10)

The high-class race is quite strong for a Tier 2 meeting, with numerous highly rated runners engaged who haven't won of late making them eligible, although many have been super consistent. The back-row runners WAZZA (8) and ANOTHER NIEN (9) have been consistently placing in stronger fields than what they meet here and, with any luck in running, should be finishing home strongly. Their chances will also rely on some genuine early tempo, where MY WAY (1), LETSGOBRO (3) and most likely IMPERIAL LAZ (7) may all be used hard off the gate with their sharp gate speed. The veteran WE SALUTE YOU (5) is racing as well as ever without winning, having been the bridesmaid at his past four starts, and is another who would appreciate plenty of tempo throughout to allow him to finish home strongly. Selections:WAZZA (8), ANOTHER NIEN (9), WE SALUTE YOU (5), IMPERIAL LAZ (7)

The final race is for the lower-win or rated mares, where we see some progressive horses engaged. CRAYONS TO PERFUME (3) has been super impressive since arriving in the state. She found the front last start and ran time that would make her very hard to run down in a race of this nature. ARDEN SEASCAPE (4) won impressively first up in the state, coming from well back in the field off a fast last half, and looks the testing material. QUETZALLI (2) is a handy three-year-old filly who also draws nicely and should look to find a position on speed. She looks the clear third pick and a genuine danger to the two favoured runners. SPORT WATCHER (1) was disappointing last start after putting together some consistent performances prior, but gets her chance to earn another cheque for connections from the pole draw. The remainder are lower-class mares who may lack the class of those mentioned above, with DOLCE DRAMA (6) looking the best of the rest after finishing runner-up at her past two starts. Selections:CRAYONS TO PERFUME (3), ARDEN SEASCAPE (4), QUETZALLI (2), SPORT WATCHER (1) Harness.org.au Help Privacy Advertise Terms Of Use Contact Us © Racing Information Services Enterprise 2026 Powered by

OVERVIEW: BLUE MIKI (2) has been in fantastic form recently after a run of placings, and he got back into the winner’s circle last start after leading at Melton. He’s a versatile horse, but his gate speed should allow him to find the front again here. SPEEDY HEALEY (5) is also in great form and has the best sectional times in this event. He won well last start at Geelong, but he does have a challenging barrier to overcome here. STERLING GIGI (9) is a two-year-old who is racing better than his numerical form suggests. He’s been racing through the Group 1 Vicbred Super Series, where he finished fifth in both his heat and semi-final before finishing sixth in the final. He has ability and a good barrier to follow through early, but he is a young horse taking on older horses here. WINGATE GUY (1) hit the line brilliantly last start to get back into the winner’s circle and finds the ideal barrier to map well again here. BACK: BLUE MIKI (2)– 2 units (win) SELECTIONS:BLUE MIKI (2), SPEEDY HEALEY (5), STERLING GIGI (9), WINGATE GUY (1)

OVERVIEW: SPUN SILVER (5) is a flashy, high-speed grey mare who is in great form, finishing in the top three at her last five starts. The first few hundred metres will be important here as she has great gate speed, but so does IAMAWINGATE (4), who is drawn inside her, although he hasn’t shown his gate speed much recently. If she does get caught in the breeze, she could be vulnerable over the middle-distance trip. MIKI MARK (9) has a barrier to follow through here and get into the running line comfortably. He’s racing well and has the best sectional times in this event. FOUR EVER A STAR (3) is having her fourth start back after three years on the sidelines. She has improved with each start back, running home well last start to be beaten only 3.7 metres. Her fitness and confidence should be good here, and we are likely to see another improved performance. IAMAWINGATE (4) is racing OK and has the gate speed to map well here. He did it tough last start at Stawell but fought on well for third. Also respecting TREACHEROUSTIMES (10) here, but he has a tricky barrier. SELECTIONS: SPUN SILVER (5),MIKI MARK (9), FOUR EVER A STAR (3),IAMAWINGATE (4).

OVERVIEW: NO MONEY NO HONEY (5) is a very talented mare, but her manners are poor more often than not. She won a Trotting Mares Free For All two starts ago at Melton when she was on her best behaviour. She needs to trot here. KEAYANG MINNESOTA (2) is a smart mare who can sometimes gallop, but there is no doubt she has the ability to be competitive in this field. If she trots safely, she can make her presence felt. KITTY CASH (4) is a progressive trotter who keeps getting better with each start. She has proven she can make her own luck and win well. This looks to be one of her toughest tests, but she continues to rise to the occasion. ALECTRONA (1) is a lightly raced trotter who has been solid and competitive in most of her runs. She broke through for her maiden victory last start very impressively. She is on the up. SELECTIONS:NO MONEY NO HONEY (5), KEAYANG MINNESOTA (2), KITTY CASH (4), ALECTRONA (1)

OVERVIEW: WAZZANT ME (3) is an interesting performer. He has good trial form, but his manners were a query in his one career start. He was very green and not tractable. That was in July, and he’s been back to the trials since, where he performed well. We will learn more about him here, but he needs to bring his best behaviour. DYGANALI (6) has been racing well. She had a tough run last start, while her two runs prior were competitive placings. She has a tricky barrier, but a win wouldn’t surprise. CHARLIE SEBASTIAN (2) has the best figure form in this event, placing a few times recently. He flashed home nicely last start at Cranbourne, but it was his run at Maryborough three starts back that really caught my eye. He flew home from last to be beaten by only a narrow margin and looks to be working towards his maiden victory. Similarly to WAZZANT ME (3), JILLIBY ECLIPSE (4) has struggled with her manners in her two career starts. However, her trials have been good. She needs to pace throughout, but she has the ability to be competitive if she puts it all together. SELECTIONS:WAZZANT ME (3), DYGANALI (6), CHARLIE SEBASTIAN (2), JILLIBY ECLIPSE (4)

OVERVIEW: ROCKNROLL RAMBO (6) moved to Victoria in July and seems to be getting better with each start. Two starts ago, he got into third after settling last, and then last start he worked to find the front and was only narrowly beaten late. He has proven he’s versatile with his race map, which is a big advantage from the tricky barrier. GOZO MAJOR (11) has the best sectional times in this field. He is tough and can do plenty of work in his races, although he did seem a little below his best last start. He will need to make his own luck from barrier 11. TOPZAVSKI (1) is first-up here but gets the ace barrier, which should give him a good trip. DELTA STARZ (9) has been racing better than her numerical form suggests. Last start, she didn’t have the clearest running late but was letting down nicely. She should get a good trip here and be saved for one run. BACK: ROCKNROLL RAMBO (2)– 2 units (win) SELECTIONS:ROCKNROLL RAMBO (6), GOZO MAJOR (11), TOPZAVSKI (1), DELTA STARZ (9)

OVERVIEW: MONEY TALKS (6) has been racing consistently well. Although beaten 22.3 metres last start, it wasn’t a bad run and he was racing in a much tougher field than this one. He has the best sectional times in this event. ALLWATFUNJINGLES (9) performs well and has a nice turn of foot when he gets things right. Barrier nine should suit him here as he has space to settle early. MAJOR MAX (5) is a trotter you need to take on trust. When he gets things right, he performs well. If he trots throughout here, he is a winning chance. BET BET HOTSHOT (7) got back into the winner’s circle last week after getting a perfect fence trip and running home well late. He’s racing in good form, but barrier seven will make it hard for him. BACK: MONEY TALKS (6) – 2 units (win) SELECTIONS:MONEY TALKS (6), ALLWATFUNJINGLES (9), MAJOR MAX (5), BET BET HOTSHOT (7)

OVERVIEW: This is a very strong race with some nice mares. SHARP INTEREST (2) is a talented type with a great turn of foot. The way she let down two starts ago at Wagga was outstanding. This is a tough race, but she gets the barrier advantage here. SHES ALLABOUTLUV (5) is one of the best mares from Tasmania, and her record speaks for itself. She got well back in her Vicbred Super Series heat last start and couldn’t make ground into the race. She will improve from that run. IDEAL MOTH (3) is a proven talented mare at her best. There are a few question marks over where she is at currently, but she will be competitive here. DELIGHTFUL MIKI (8) was held up and let down very well in her Vicbred Super Series heat and seemed unlucky not to make the final. She is a talented mare, and being the only horse on the back row, she has some map options. KEAYANG VIPER (7) is a smart mare in great form who is lightly raced. However, she has a challenging barrier here against a strong field of mares, and this is her toughest test. BACK: SHARP INTEREST (2)– 2 units (win) SELECTIONS:SHES ALLABOUTLUV (5), SHARP INTEREST (2), DELIGHTFUL MIKI (8), IDEAL MOTH (3)

OVERVIEW: KIMBERLEYS TREE (8) has her quirks, but she also has plenty of ability. She galloped out last start and charged home into second, even after missing away by a few lengths. Being the only horse on the second line, she has space and time to settle early. If she trots throughout, she will be hard to beat. I AM HARRO (3) is a nice trotter when he brings his best. I can’t leave him out of a race like this one. MASSIF CENTRAL (1) is in good form, winning last start after getting a fence trip. He is likely to map similarly here. KYVALLEY MISTY (6) has had issues with her manners throughout her career, but she’s putting it together now and is in career-best form. Also respecting VAN DOREN (2) and JESSICAS STORY (4) here. BACK: KIMBERLEYS TREE (8) – 2 units (win) SELECTIONS:KIMBERLEYS TREE (8), I AM HARRO (3), MASSIF CENTRAL (1), KYVALLEY MISTY (6)

OVERVIEW: ZIPPIN PAST (8) is a smart two-year-old filly taking on the older horses here. She usually uses her fast gate speed to map positively, but she won’t be able to do that from barrier eight, so we will see a different racing style from her here. She has a great turn of foot and was third last start in the Group 1 Vicbred Super Series Final. DONA AMALIA (6) is better than her recent numerical form suggests. She has had a run of bad luck or poor manners, but she is a very fast mare who has the ability to make her own luck and race tough. CARTACALHA (5) has shown promise throughout her career. She did underperform last start, but likely had excuses. She’s a winning chance here at her best. CHRISTMAS BABE (1) is a ten-year-old mare with great gate speed who likes to lead. Her fitness is a query here as she is first-up. SELECTIONS:ZIPPIN PAST (8), DONA AMALIA (6), CARTACALHA (5), CHRISTMAS BABE (1)

OVERVIEW: This is a nice field of trotters to end the card. MUSKEE (6) was slightly below his best late last start in his Vicbred Super Series heat, although he did get a long way back in a tough field when they ran home in quick time. He is a very nice trotter who looks like he will continue to progress through his grades. His win four starts ago at Melton was outstanding when he sustained a long run. At his best, he’s a talented and versatile trotter. CLAUDYS HERO (2) is a talented trotter with a bright future, but he can get it wrong with his manners. He galloped last start in his Vicbred Super Series heat. He does have the gate speed to map well here and, if he finds the fence, he will be hard to run down. VOLDAGHA (3) is another promising trotter who can perform well at his best. He is first-up here. KYVALLEY JAGGER (1) gets the ace barrier to use to his advantage here, and he’s racing well when he trots throughout. Also keeping an eye on THATS MY CARDIGAN (5), who does have a nice turn of foot and good gate speed, but this is a tough step up. SELECTIONS:MUSKEE (6), CLAUDYS HERO (2), VOLDAGHA (3), KYVALLEY JAGGER (1) Harness.org.au Help Privacy Advertise Terms Of Use Contact Us © Racing Information Services Enterprise 2026 Powered by

A maiden for two and three-year-old fillies kicks off tonight, where BETTYS GIRL (3) looks to have the best of the exposed form. She produced a nice third on debut earlier this year after showing gate speed and, while she hasn't trialled since, that form would be hard to beat here. Her stablemate CHASING THE ACE (4) was a trial winner last week and looks the best of the debutants. RAZZAMATAZ (1) is an extremely well-bred filly out of the smart mare Benediction and is a half-sister to Inter Dominion placegetter Nyack. She ran an okay second in a trial a month ago and you'd expect she has come on since then, so betting may be the best guide. FARRAHS LEGACY (2) is the other two-year-old on debut and has been hit and miss with its manners at the trials, making it somewhat hard to gauge. BELLAS ANGEL (5) is the most experienced horse in the field with four starts and has improved at her past two starts against older horses, so must also be considered. Selections:BETTYS GIRL (3), CHASING THE ACE (4), RAZZAMATAZ (1), BELLAS ANGEL (5)

A small but competitive field for the No More Than Four Wins horses, where OUR WILLOW (1) gets the pole draw and produced a nice effort first up for the new stable. She possesses good gate speed, although suspect she may take a sit on WEE GEORGIE WOOD (2), who won in fast time over the mile last start and is a super-consistent pacer. ROCKY STRIDE (4) has been racing well without winning and should again be right in the finish after competing in some handy three-year-old races of late. BEARHUNTA (5) went around as favourite last week but broke on the first turn. He clearly possesses plenty of ability if he brings his best manners here. DENVER MAN (6) won impressively first up in the state when doing all the work in okay time. This is a slight rise in grade, but he certainly can't be discounted. Selections:OUR WILLOW (1), ROCKY STRIDE (4), WEE GEORGIE WOOD (2), , BEARHUNTA (5)

CUZZY BRO (1) led against most of these runners last start and was simply too good in exceptional time, despite not being favoured in the market. A similar run from the pole draw again should see him extremely hard to beat. BETTABLACK TIGER (3) tried to make ground from back in the field in that race and battled on okay. GO THE RED (6) should again be right in the finish, especially if he can secure some cover into the race, having been super consistent of late. WATERMELON SUGAR (4) and VANQUISH STRIDE (5) have been filling the placings in similar-class races and should be thereabouts again, although it is hard to see them beating the favoured runners. Selections:CUZZY BRO (1), BETTABLACK TIGER (3) , GO THE RED (6), WATERMELON SUGAR (4)

A couple of handy three-year-olds in JILLSTIGER (1) and A DRAGON FOR JOE (3) take on the older horses here, along with SOHO TIGER LILY (2), who possesses sharp gate speed and should be looking to be first to the pegs. She should be well suited by the mile distance. OUR SWEET TRIXIE (4) showed good gate speed to lead and win in nice time last start and will no doubt again press forward from the middle front-row draw. TALK IS CHEAP (6) and GOBSMACKED (8) will be relying on some genuine tempo throughout to allow them to finish home strongly and get into the finish. Selections: A DRAGON FOR JOE (3), JILLSTIGER (1), GOBSMACKED (8), OUR SWEET TRIXIE (4)

A full field assembles for the No More Than One Lifetime Win race, where QUARTEIRA (12) starts from the outside draw after causing a false start in the score-up last time. He clearly has untapped ability and, although he faces a difficult draw, the 2200-metre journey should give him the opportunity to show his class. If he brings his best behaviour, he will be hard to hold out late. The remainder looks a fairly even bunch, with WINNING BREW (5) producing nice performances at its past two starts that are good enough to see her run a race again, although she strikes an awkward draw. SWEETHEART DIOR (4) is in a similar boat and will no doubt be looking to find a forward position. OMYBACNKNEESJUDGE (10) have been consistent of late from favourable front-row draws. It would be somewhat surprising to see the others take this out, with the exception of SNIPER SANZ (11), who resumes from a long break and did show some nice ability at times as a two-year-old. Selections:QUARTEIRA (12), WINNING BREW (5), SWEETHEART DIOR (4), SNIPER SANZ (11)

There should be speed aplenty here, with numerous fast beginners drawn across the front row. WEONA EAGLE (1) draws the pole so should find a nice position in the run. KEEPERS IDEAL (6), MUZZAME MATE (4), MIGHT AND TEMERITY (3) and INTO THE HARKNESS (2) should all look to push forward from their front-row draws, which should ensure a solid tempo throughout. It's a very hard race to assess, where the runner that gets the nicest run in transit may ultimately be the one to beat. IDEN LADY LINCOLN (7) could be the one to benefit if she brings her best form after producing a nice trial ahead of her return, and should be running home strongly. Selections:IDEN LADY LINCOLN (7), WEONA EAGLE (1), MUZZAME MATE (4), KEEPERS IDEAL (6)

TAMBROS TILLY (7) was an impressive winner last start after settling midfield, but draws the outside of the front row here, which makes her task harder in what looks a very even field overall. GOODTIME OSCAR (9) is a consistent pacer and gets a nice trailing back-row draw, which should give him every opportunity. WILL HE PIKE (5) may look to use his handy gate speed to attempt to find the pegs, or at least secure a forward position from the middle front-row draw. LYNRYD SKYNRYD (6) will no doubt press forward from the gate but hasn't been finishing his races off as well of late. MERRYWOOD PAUL (1) should appreciate stepping back up to the middle-distance journey and is going better than his form suggests, so he could be the one from the nice draw if the gaps appear late. Selections:TAMBROS TILLY (7), GOODTIME OSCAR (9), MERRYWOOD PAUL (1), WILL HE PIKE (5)

The low-class race of the night brings together a field with no clear standout form. ALL ABOUT SADIE (1) again draws well courtesy of having just the one lifetime win and should get every chance if the gaps appear late. DANCINWIVJOLENE (3) resumes from a break but has shown enough ability at times to suggest that, at her best, she could take this out. MIKI SANZ (6) drops back in grade after being thereabouts of late without having much luck in her races, although she again strikes an awkward draw. CHRIS BE QUICK (9) gets the nice trailing back-row draw and is always capable of running home strongly, so could be the one they have to hold out late. Selections:ALL ABOUT SADIE (1), DANCINWIVJOLENE (3), MIKI SANZ (6), CHRIS BE QUICK (9)

There should be some good gate speed and a genuine tempo early over the mile, with JUST LIKA DREAM (4) looking to hold a forward position while trying to hold out IFYOULOVEMELETMEGO (5) and REPETITIVE (6), who are both sharp off the gate when asked. IMA LITTLE NEEDY (1) has been below his best of late but could improve significantly from the pole draw, and his best form would make him hard to beat here. ROSE NOIRE (8) will need some luck to come her way but got a deserved victory on the board last start and should again be thereabouts.
